speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in light of the number of workplace fatalities in 2024 and the implementation of the Safety Time-out in November 2024, how effective has this measure been in raising safety awareness within the industry; and (b) what additional steps can the Ministry take to further enhance safety awareness and ensure compliance with workplace safety regulations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower with regard to the spike in workplace fatalities in the construction section in the second half of 2024 (a) how many active construction sites participated in the Safety Time-out called by the Ministry in November 2024; (b) whether the Ministry has analysed if there were any specific reasons behind the sharp rise in workplace fatalities; and (c) how does the Ministry intend to address this concerning trend.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) of the 15 construction workplace deaths in the second half of 2024, how many have involved companies that have been allowed to resume work after only completing general safety reviews following earlier serious incidents; (b) whether the Ministry will automatically require external safety audits and specific structural changes to be implemented before work can resume at sites with fatalities given this stricter approach have successfully reduced deaths during the 2022 heightened safety period; and (c) if not, why not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition, I will address two oral PQs scheduled for the Sitting on 8 January 2025 by Mr Patrick Tay1 and Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These five PQs relate to construction workplace fatalities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: I will respond to these questions together, so that I can give a comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These worksites were required to undertake measures, such as reviewing their safety management systems, before they can resume work.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I share the Members' concern about the increase in workplace fatalities, especially in the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While the sector’s Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) performance is better than those of many developed countries like Japan, we are not yet on par with top performers such as the Netherlands.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There is certainly scope for our construction sector to do better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has continued to tighten our enforcement efforts for the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: More recently, we instituted a Safety Time-out in November 2024 to refresh workers’ awareness of WSH practices and reinforce the importance of adhering to safety protocols.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The requirement for external safety audits to be conducted following serious lapses remains in effect after the Heightened Safety Period.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To strengthen accountability at the leadership level, we have also instituted measures such as requiring Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) and board directors in the higher-risk sectors, including construction, to attend the Top Executive WSH Programme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the companies and the workers in the sector can certainly do better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On our part, we will monitor the progress of the measures implemented this year to further improve safety and accountability.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I urge all employers and workers to remain alert as we approach the Chinese New Year period, which is typically a time when companies face time pressures to complete projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM will continue with enhanced enforcement efforts during this period.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is our collective responsibility to ensure that every worker returns home safely.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While I appreciate the Senior Minister of State's reply on the multi-agency approach for the Safety Time-out, my question is more on the effectiveness, or at least, increasing the effectiveness of the Safety Time-out.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the MOM website, during a Safety Time-out, companies are strongly urged to review their risk assessment and debrief their workforce.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can I suggest that during the Safety Time-out, companies are required to review their risk assessment, their safety management system and required to acknowledge that they have done so, especially at the leadership level, whether it is from the directors, and within the companies, flow it down, with their workers acknowledging that they have been debriefed and they are sure of the safe practices that are required?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Indeed, the Safety Time-out that was done was voluntary because this was meant to complement MOM's enforcement efforts overall.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In terms of effectiveness, a Safety Time-out on its own is not going to be the panacea to solve the fatality issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That has put a lot of companies on notice because they know that if something happens, there is record, there is video surveillance that is there as evidence for MOM to investigate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That has deterred many companies in terms of making sure that all processes and protocols are in place.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The other things which I mentioned earlier on include, we have now required CEOs and board directors in industries – not just construction but others as well – to refresh themselves to be very familiar.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the accountability is not just at the worker level, but at CEO and board level, so that they cannot say, "I didn't know.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: My safety officer was already hired to do this." Accountability starts from the top.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is none of this old business of telling us, "This was some sub-contractor down the line, I have no sight, no visibility".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: You have to be accountable for all your sub-contractors down the line.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have made some measures, apart from just the Safety Time-out, that we think should enhance the safety protocols and procedures in the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We worked very closely with MND and BCA on this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think one aspect would also be how we transform the sector, which MND and BCA are playing a very important role in this too, in terms of making our construction processes more productive, more safe.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, you can see many of them performing quite well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some of them have gone beyond just video surveillance and to include video analytics into the surveillance systems which are able to proactively predict or pre-empt some of these unsafe things in workers' conduct.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, I think we have to not just rely on Safety Time-outs, but on the whole suite of measures that we introduced last year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And give us time, because it has been about six months or so for some of these measures and they need time to permeate and for us to evaluate their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I assure Members that we are doing all we can, but the industry will also need to respond, and so, give them time to do so.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I agree with the Senior Minister of State that we must step up our efforts to improve safety in the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Were these primarily by large construction projects or by small- and medium-sized projects?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I recall that there was a period of time when there were many sub-contractors working within the same worksite.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And if there is a clear trend, we should double down on our efforts to engage the specific sub-sector so as to better address the rise in the construction-related work fatalities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I do not have the statistics off-hand in terms of the mix between large and small firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I can tell the Member that based on our analysis in previous years for this particular group, there is a mix in terms of large and small firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If you think about it, many of these could have been avoided because many of them are in the addition and alteration (A&A) type of projects and renovation works, and some are doing maintenance works in facilities management.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are the areas in which we are working with BCA to see how we can encourage and better educate to create better awareness and procedures and protocols among our small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, yes, there are the larger firms but if you think about risk profile, larger worksites, bigger workforce, but the numbers are over-represented if you think about ratios in the SME sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And that is one area in which we are working closely with BCA to try to manage.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first supplementary question is in relation to the point that he mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I am not sure whether I heard correctly about there being a temporary bar from public sector projects should there be certain violations.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In the context of workplace fatalities, for example, we all agree that it is one too many.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, would workplace deaths, for example, automatically trigger such a certain period of disqualification and how would these be assessed?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is in relation to the SnapSAFE reports.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I note in a news article that there was an increase in the number of such workplace safety violation reports.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of the level of resources that MOM has, is it adequately staffed, to ensure that these are properly investigated and, not just the investigation, but also the subsequent follow-up to make sure that the rectifications are done to prevent any incidents?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I would say that we think this would be effective because the public sector does take on more than half of the construction projects in Singapore and therefore, I think that is a big, sizeable account for many of our construction firms, especially larger ones.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I said, one of the key things we got to look out for are the SMEs, because they may not rely on public sector works and typically, they are over-represented when we think about some of the A&A renovation projects or even facility management projects that result in fatalities or major injuries.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think that is one area in which the disqualification credit may not have happened and that is probably one reason why you find that many of our larger firms tend to do better too.
